A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same survey, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. V2's Appendix A is an earlier revision log; v4 removes that log while retaining the scientific material it describes.

before.justification: V2 presents a technical survey with taxonomies, illustrative prompts and pseudocode. Performance and efficiency findings in Sections 8.3–8.4 are attributed to other studies; Appendix A reports no original empirical results.

after.justification: V4 remains a technical survey. Its added introductory findings are attributed to prior literature, and it reports no original experiments, simulations, user studies or empirical data analysis.

M1.justification: The LLM-profiled roles, modular search procedures and framework descriptions in Sections 3–5 are retained. Repositioned pseudocode does not introduce an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: The task and benchmark catalogue in Table 2 is unchanged. PlanBench and SearchBench appear in new introductory discussion, but neither version conducts a new training or evaluation exercise on these benchmarks.

E2.justification: Table 7 retains the same reviewed frameworks. Section 8.3 also retains the cited comparisons of ToT and RAP against CoT and self-consistency; no empirical comparator set is revised.

E3.justification: No experimental splits, metrics, budgets, sample sizes or testing procedures are added or revised. The retained descriptions of settings in surveyed work are unchanged.

E4.justification: No ablation, robustness experiment or empirical case study is added or removed. Existing prompting illustrations and cited failure cases remain; the deleted appendix contains only revision history.

E5.justification: Neither version adds or removes run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained discussions of model confidence and self-consistency describe methods rather than experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V4's introduction adds literature-attributed qualitative findings about near-saturated language-reasoning performance and poorer-than-human performance on PlanBench and SearchBench. Existing Section 8.3 rankings and Section 8.4's cited 10–20-times slowdown, especially below 90% evaluator accuracy, remain unchanged. No original measurements are added.

T1.justification: The MDP formulations, UCT/PUCT equations, backpropagation expressions and A* definitions are unchanged, as are the admissibility and Bellman-property discussions. Visual inspection confirms that the apparent difference in Procedure 5 is an extraction-order artifact.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a unified MDP-based task formulation and modular comparison of LLM roles and search frameworks. Explicitly naming MDPs in v4's abstract restates a contribution already established in v2.

C2.justification: The new introduction adds the cited hypothesis that strong language reasoning may reflect reasoning paths present in training corpora, contrasting this with non-NLP planning difficulty. Section 8.4 also refines tree attention's description from eliminating redundant I/O to reducing memory I/O. Existing applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the documented update-resource pointer from the LLM-Agent-Survey repository's search.md to the LLM-Search repository. Implementation explanations and pseudocode otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds introductory references on language models, prompting and reasoning benchmarks, including Achiam et al. (2023), Kojima et al. (2022) and Borazjanizadeh et al. (2024). The main framework catalogue and related-work organization remain intact.

P1.justification: V4 expands the opening motivation, edits the abstract, consolidates the audience and use-case material, and removes Appendix A's historical change log. These are localized revisions; the technical sections retain their structure and wording.

P2.justification: Existing tables and pseudocode are repositioned relative to the prose, including Tables 3, 4 and 6 and Procedure 8. V4 adds publication headers and reflows the pages, while retaining Figure 1 and the substantive table contents.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's brief opening, v4 better explains why search matters differently for language reasoning and non-NLP planning, helping readers interpret the retained taxonomy. Additional contextual references and consolidated introductory material modestly improve orientation. The technical substance and existing empirical support remain largely unchanged.
